directive.name: coding
directive.description: Code quality standards: architecture, type safety, and documentation

context.principle: Policy belongs in orchestrators, mechanism in capabilities
Dependencies must form a DAG (no circular dependencies). Flow is inward: Computer <- Capability <- Orchestrator
Every module must be categorized with suffix: .computer.ts, .capability.ts, .orchestrator.ts
Orchestrators should be decomposed when: >300 lines, >2-3 unrelated concerns, or distinct domains emerge
Entry points (e.g., extension.ts) should be thin composition roots that wire domain orchestrators together
Never use any - use unknown and narrow with type guards
All exported functions must have explicit return types
Use branded types for domain identifiers (TaskId, ProjectId, etc.)
Use discriminated unions for states, not boolean flags
All exported symbols must have TSDoc documentation
TSDoc must use multi-line format, not single-line
@param tags must use hyphen separator: @param name - description
No backwards compatibility - break things and fix them properly
No deprecation notices - delete or keep, no middle ground
All code changes must pass build verification before completion

This project builds festinalente. The .claude/ and .opencode/ directories contain built output from apps/festinalente/src/content/ — never modify them directly. Edit source files in apps/festinalente/src/content/.

process.rule: Identify which architectural layer each affected file belongs to and verify dependency DAG is maintained
Categorize every new module with correct suffix
When creating pure functions, wrap them in a computer factory
Identify distinct domains and plan orchestrator structure before implementation
Create domain orchestrators in orchestrators/ directory when adding new domains
Verify orchestrator size - if >300 lines, plan decomposition into domain orchestrators
Define domain types for new identifiers using branded types
Use readonly on value objects and interface properties
Use options objects for functions with more than 2 parameters
Add TSDoc to all exported functions, classes, interfaces, and types
Scan for forbidden patterns before any manual review
Check architectural classification of all new/modified modules
Run all relevant build commands for modified packages
Verify each task step with appropriate build command
When modifying skills, templates, or partials, edit files in apps/festinalente/src/content/ (not .claude/ or .opencode/).

check.expect: Festina Lente package builds successfully (exit code 0)

check.reason: Capabilities cannot import other capabilities (lateral dependency)
Orchestrators cannot import other orchestrators (use composition root)

check.item: Orchestrator files are under 300 lines (decompose if larger)
Entry point (extension.ts) is a thin composition root
Distinct domains have their own orchestrators in orchestrators/
Domain orchestrators don't import each other directly

check.reason: any type disables type checking - use unknown and narrow
as any is an escape hatch - fix the underlying type issue
ts-ignore suppresses errors - fix the type issue or link to issue
Single-line TSDoc on exports - use multi-line format
Banner/divider comments are noise, not documentation
@param missing hyphen separator - use @param name - description
No deprecation notices - delete or keep, no middle ground

check.item: Dependency graph forms a DAG (no circular dependencies)
All new modules have correct suffix (.computer.ts, .capability.ts, .orchestrator.ts)
No policy logic in capabilities
Computers only import other computers
Orchestrators under 300 lines (decompose if larger)
Entry point is thin composition root (wiring only)
Distinct domains have separate orchestrators
Domain orchestrators don't import each other
No any type in new code
All exported functions have explicit return types
Domain types used for IDs (not raw strings)
Discriminated unions for states (not boolean flags)
All exported symbols have TSDoc
Multi-line TSDoc format used
@param tags include hyphen separator
No @deprecated tags - delete unused code
No backwards compatibility shims or wrappers
No feature flags for old vs new behavior

example.explanation: Capability decides WHEN to create - this is policy, belongs in orchestrator
Capability provides mechanism (createSession), orchestrator decides when (getSession)
Lateral dependency - both capabilities should be injected into orchestrator
any disables type checking, making access unsafe
unknown requires proper type narrowing before use
Branded types prevent mixing up different ID types
Boolean flags allow impossible states (isLoading AND isComplete both true)
Only one state is possible at a time, enabling exhaustive handling
Single-line format is not proper TSDoc
Delete oldFunction, update all callers to use newFunction
No deprecation period, just direct updates
No compatibility layers - migrate all data to new format
Split into domain orchestrators when >300 lines or >2-3 unrelated concerns
Thin composition root with domain orchestrators in orchestrators/
Domain orchestrator owns policy for one domain, uses factory DI
Orchestrators should not import each other - wire them via composition root
